judged_text: In deleteEvent, the same broken pattern: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find can never match and calendarId is always undefined. Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId no longer deletes the event from the booking's destination calendar (old code used destinationCalendar.externalId); the delete call gets calendarId undefined and the remote Google Calendar event is orphaned, leaving busy slots blocked on the attendee/organizer calendar.

Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId no longer deletes the event from the booking's destination calendar (old code used destinationCalendar.externalId); the delete call gets calendarId undefined and the remote Google Calendar event is orphaned, leaving busy slots blocked on the attendee/organizer calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` change the fallback calendar selection to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. In that branch `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, so the `.find(...)` predicate can’t match a real destination calendar externalId, yielding `undefined`. `deleteEvent` then falls back to `defaultCalendarId = "primary"`, so events created on a non-primary destination calendar won’t be deleted when a booking reference lacks `externalCalendarId` (old code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). This can orphan remote events.
